items.content_html:
The most important part of this PR is fixing the log provider. We were earlier giving the wrong -t flag to journalctl, making it so that sshguard wouldn't get the relevant logs it needed to inspect. This has been resolved by expanding the type of the option, allowing for both -u and -t flags.

The default has been set so the service will work out of the box by setting services.sshguard.enable = true

Other notable things done:

  • removed bash wrappers around pre exec post exec hooks
  • split log provider into separate service, allowing for easier debugging and split hardening privileges.
  • automatically handle socket activated sshd
  • add myself as module maintainer
  • systemd hardening
  • added nixos test

items.content_html:
Resolves #445117, supersedes #401080 & #449578.

K3s and RKE2 share a lot of functionality, but since the nixpkgs RKE2 maintainer team is much smaller than K3s', its module tends to fall far behind - and for feature parity, code duplication across the two modules would be needed (see #401080). Merging them should make it possible for the RKE2 module to keep up with K3s without having maintainers manually copy code over.

I haven't removed or added any options, this PR is more or less just a (big) refactor. I also haven't tested the K3s module manually, but all tests in nixos/tests/{k3s,rke2} passed and I'm currently using the RKE2 module to host my site with no issues.

I've also added myself as a maintainer to RKE2.

Maintainer cc:
@rorosen @zimbatm @stefan-bordei
@NixOS/k3s

Add the following warning:

Since version 1.52.0 Tailscale creates a firewall rule that accepts all incoming traffic on its interface. This effectively disables the NixOS firewall on this interface.

To disable this warning explicitly add the Tailscale interface to the firewall's trustedInterfaces:

networking.firewall.trustedInterfaces = [ config.services.tailscale.interfaceName ];

tailscale/tailscale@ba6ec42

items.content_html:
In my case the closure was already symlinked and when the activation service ran before switching root, it would fail, causing the system to not be able to leave the first stage, saying "Switch root target does not contain usable init".

On regular, mutable NixOS systems this is usually not an issue, however, when building read-only images where /nix/store is mounted to /sysroot/nix/store, edge cases like this are more likely to happen.
